questions.stem: This diagram shows the layered anatomy of the pericardium. Excess fluid accumulating in the space between the visceral and parietal pericardium, compressing the heart, defines which condition?

explanation.summary: The space labeled between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal pericardium is the pericardial cavity. When fluid there accumulates rapidly or in large volume it compresses the chambers and impairs filling, producing cardiac tamponade, a life-threatening cause of obstructive shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: The space labeled between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal pericardium is the pericardial cavity. questions.stem: A patient in cardiogenic shock has this chest radiograph. Which hemodynamic abnormality best explains the pulmonary findings shown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated right atrial pressure with clear lung fields

explanation.summary: The diffuse perihilar interstitial opacities represent pulmonary edema, which develops when elevated left-sided filling pressures (a high pulmonary capillary wedge pressure reflecting elevated left atrial pressure) force fluid into the alveoli. This is why IV fluids can worsen hypoxia in cardiogenic shock.

questions.stem: This ECG rhythm strip shows beat-to-beat variation in QRS complex amplitude. This finding is most specific for which condition?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Large pericardial effusion with cardiac tamponade

explanation.summary: The alternating high- and low-voltage QRS complexes are electrical alternans, produced by the swinging motion of the heart within a large fluid-filled pericardial sac. It is the most specific ECG finding for a large pericardial effusion causing tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: The alternating high- and low-voltage QRS complexes are electrical alternans, produced by the swinging motion of the heart within a large fluid-filled pericardial sac. It is the most specific ECG finding for a large pericardial effusion causing tamponade.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph was obtained from a hypotensive patient, and its findings are considered a contraindication to intravenous fluid administration. What abnormality does the film demonstrate?

explanation.summary: The radiograph shows engorged central pulmonary vessels and hazy interstitial markings characteristic of pulmonary edema. In a shock patient, radiographic pulmonary edema with hypoxia signals fluid overload, so IV fluids should be withheld rather than given.
explanation.whyCorrect: The radiograph shows engorged central pulmonary vessels and hazy interstitial markings characteristic of pulmonary edema. In a shock patient, radiographic pulmonary edema with hypoxia signals fluid overload, so IV fluids should be withheld rather than given.
